verdict.rationale: ROS 2 provides the underlying transport/QoS infrastructure (tunable reliability, best-effort/UDP-like modes for lossy networks, pub/sub topics, actions with feedback) that a teleop stack could be built on, and community notes confirm teleop is one of the 'free' ecosystem capabilities (ros2-comm-9). However there is no first-party evidence of an integrated live-video pipeline, joystick/teleop packages, or end-to-end responsive control demonstration, and community feedback flags real-time/timing weaknesses and general difficulty deploying robust systems over real networks (ros2-comm-6, ros2-comm-11, ros2-comm-12). missing for 10: dedicated video streaming/compression integration, an official teleop package (e.g., teleop_twist) referenced in evidence, latency/responsiveness benchmarks over real-world (lossy/WAN) networks, and independent hands-on confirmation of a full live teleoperation demo.
